paper_metadata.title: The Effect of g' Content on the Densities of Ni-Based Superalloys

evidence.quote: Ni-based superalloys are used in gas turbine engines for both aircraft and power generation. These alloys contain a large number of elements, which can be divided into three groups: (1) Ni, Cr, Co, and Fe; (2) heavy metals, W, Re, Ta, Mo, Nb, etc.; and (3) Al.
Dr. Rainer Wunderlich (Ulm University) for supplying the density data on Ni-based superalloys.

Al imparts further strength by the formation of the g9 phase (an ordered precipitate possessing L12 crystal structure), which prevents the movement of dislocations. In these alloys, the g9 phase can be considered as Ni 3Al or (Ni, Co) 3(Al, Ti).

mechanisms.name: strong Ni-Al bonding in solid and liquid

evidence.quote: The strong bonding between Ni and Al in superalloys is still present in the liquid and results in higher densities than those calculated from ideal mixing rules
the coarsening of the g9 phase is associated with a marked increase in slope for group 2 and 3 alloys, which contain significant amounts of the g9 phase
